title: How to Hire a Home Improvement Contractor: The Complete Checklist
meta_title: How to Hire a Home Improvement Contractor — NYC Checklist
meta_description: Definitive checklist for hiring a home improvement contractor in NYC. License verification, insurance, contracts, red flags.
excerpt: The definitive checklist for hiring a home improvement contractor in NYC and Long Island.
body:
Verification Checklist

License: In NYC, any contractor performing home improvement work over $200 must hold an HIC license from DCWP. Verify at the DCWP website. On Long Island, verify county registration.

Insurance: General liability ($1M+ per occurrence) and workers comp. Ask for certificates. Same-day delivery is the standard.

References: Three from projects completed in the last 12 months. Call them.

Contract Essentials

NYC law requires written contracts for jobs over $500: detailed scope, total price with payment schedule (never more than 33% deposit), start/completion dates, warranty terms, 3-day cancellation right.

Red Flags

More than one-third deposit (violates NYC HIC regulations). No license number. No written contract. Pressure to sign immediately. No recent references.
